Single-Domain Generalized Object Detection (S-DGOD) aims to generalize from a
single source domain to unseen domains under distribution shifts. Existing efforts
mainly focus on simulating unseen domains or suppressing domain-specific factors.
However, they largely overlook the intrinsic generalization capability embedded
in Vision Foundation Models (VFMs). In this work, we show that unconstrained
fine-tuning disrupts the geometric structure of pre-trained representations, which
encodes domain-invariant semantics. Motivated by this, we proposeGeometric-
InvarianceFine-Tuning (GIFT), a geometric-aware fine-tuning method for VFMs.
Specifically, we introduce a series of learnable Householder reflections to the
pre-trained weights to encourage geometry-consistent adaptation under domain
shift. In addition, we propose a lightweight channel-wise scaling to facilitate

evidence.excerpt:
adaptation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GIFT
outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) approaches on two S-DGOD benchmarks.
Notably, by introducing fewer than 1% additional trainable parameters into the
frozen backbone, the proposed method achieves improvements of +7.9% and +2.9%
in mPC over the previous SOTA on the Cityscapes-C and Diverse Weather Dataset,
respectively. This finding highlights that preserving representation geometry is
crucial for robust domain generalization, establishing GIFT as a principled and
efficient solution to domain shift. The code is available at https://github.com/
zhangyin1996/GIFT.

In particular, theℓ 2 norm and pairwise distances remain invariant:

These properties ensure that R rotates the parameter space without altering its geometry, thereby

stable optimization, we employ a residual update mechanism. Specifically, we first compute the

DWDcomprises five scenarios: Daytime-Sunny (DS.), Daytime-Foggy (DF.), Dusk-Rainy (DR.),
Night-Rainy (NR.), and Night-Sunny (NS.).Cityscapes-Cis a benchmark for evaluating detection
robustness under common corruptions. It generates 15 corruption types with 5 severity levels.

mean Performance under Corruption (mPC) to evaluate robustness. For DWD [51], mPC is computed
as the average mAP over four weather conditions, while for Cityscapes-C [35], it averages mAP50
across all corruption types and severity levels.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline gains are measured on distinct unseen target domains and corruption severities with standard ground-truth labels, and the method is additionally validated across multiple VFM backbones and a semantic segmentation task.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard mAP50 and mPC metrics computed on held-out unseen corruption and adverse-weather test sets using ground-truth annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised detection losses computed only on the source-domain training sets (clean Cityscapes and Daytime-Sunny DWD), with no target-domain data or labels used during training.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported experimental numbers directly substantiate the claimed improvements (+7.9% mPC on Cityscapes-C and +2.9% mPC on DWD over prior state-of-the-art) with less than 1% trainable parameters. Ablation studies support the isolated benefits of both geometric preservation and channel scaling.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical evaluation is extensive, testing on standard S-DGOD benchmarks (Cityscapes-C and Diverse Weather Dataset) across multiple detector heads (Faster R-CNN and DINO) and multiple foundation models (DINOv2, EVA-02, SAM). Comparisons with existing PEFT methods and traditional generalization techniques show consistent gains in mPC and mAP50, corroborated by component ablations and domain-generalized semantic segmentation experiments.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on standard ground-truth labeled test sets across distinct unseen domains and corruptions without target-domain adaptation during training.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard object detection metrics (mAP50 and mPC) evaluated on held-out unseen adverse weather conditions and synthetic corruption datasets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard supervised object detection losses computed exclusively on the source domain training set (e.g., clean Cityscapes or Daytime-Sunny DWD).

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly address limitations, noting performance sensitivity when pre-trained representations are misaligned with downstream domains (such as infrared or remote sensing), residual GPU memory footprints from large backbones, and the restriction to closed-vocabulary detection setups.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is mathematically grounded and clearly specified, detailing how orthogonal Householder matrices preserve inner products and vector distances alongside residual gating and learnable diagonal channel scaling. Implementation specifics regarding target layers, rotation rank, trainable block numbers, and optimization settings are comprehensively documented.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-motivated parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique backed by formal linear algebra foundations and thorough benchmarking against relevant baselines. The experimental validation is transparent, ablated across architectures and datasets, and clearly demonstrates stated performance gains without methodological circularity.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces GIFT (Geometric-Invariance Fine-Tuning), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach for Vision Foundation Models applied to single-domain generalized object detection (S-DGOD). GIFT couples learnable Householder reflections on frozen attention weights with channel-wise scaling to preserve pre-trained representation geometry while adapting task features.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-motivated parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique backed by formal linear algebra foundations and thorough benchmarking against relevant baselines. The experimental validation is transparent, ablated across architectures and datasets, and clearly demonstrates stated performance gains without methodological circularity.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly address limitations, noting performance sensitivity when pre-trained representations are misaligned with downstream domains (such as infrared or remote sensing), residual GPU memory footprints from large backbones, and the restriction to closed-vocabulary detection setups.
